cases.name: single-word
cases.notes: §1.2: one bareword → one quoted token.

cases.name: two-words-implicit-and
cases.notes: Whitespace-separated tokens, joined by single spaces (FTS5 implicit AND).

cases.name: slash-path-is-one-token
cases.notes: `guides/onboarding` is one quoted token; the tokenizer splits on `/`, so it is an AND of two terms.

cases.name: phrase-then-prefix
cases.notes: The README example: a quoted phrase stays a phrase, a trailing `*` on a bareword becomes a prefix.

cases.name: unclosed-quote-runs-to-end
cases.notes: A missing closing quote: the phrase runs to the end of the input.

cases.name: prefix-star
cases.notes: The `*` is stripped and re-appended outside the quotes.

cases.name: star-alone-dropped
cases.notes: A bare `*` has no letter or digit once stripped → dropped → empty.

cases.name: double-star-strips-one
cases.notes: Only the last `*` is a prefix marker; the inner one stays in the quoted token.

cases.name: star-in-middle-kept
cases.notes: `*` is only special at the end of a bareword.

cases.name: punctuation-only-dropped
cases.notes: Tokens with no Unicode letter or digit are dropped; nothing survives → empty.

cases.name: punctuation-inside-kept
cases.notes: A token with letters keeps its punctuation (the tokenizer strips it later).

cases.name: quote-inside-bareword-splits
cases.notes: A `"` ends a bareword and starts a phrase: barewords and phrases can never contain a quote, so the `""` doubling rule is unreachable (§8 candidate).

cases.name: quotes-never-nest
cases.notes: `"a "b" c"` is phrase `a `, bareword `b`, phrase ` c`.

cases.name: phrase-punctuation-only-dropped
cases.notes: A phrase with no letter or digit is dropped.

cases.name: phrase-adjacent-bareword
cases.notes: A bareword may follow a closing quote without whitespace.

cases.name: unicode-letters-kept
cases.notes: Unicode `L` counts as a word character.

cases.name: unicode-digits-kept
cases.notes: Unicode `N` (here Arabic-Indic digits) counts as a word character.

cases.name: fts5-operators-neutralized
cases.notes: AND/OR/NOT/NEAR are plain quoted tokens, never operators.
cases.input: NOT apple AND pie OR NEAR

cases.name: column-filter-neutralized
cases.notes: A `col:term` is one quoted token, not a column filter.

cases.name: mixed-whitespace
cases.notes: Tabs and newlines are separators (`\s`).

cases.name: empty-input
cases.notes: Empty in, empty out.

cases.name: whitespace-only
cases.notes: Only separators → empty.
